title: What has Michael Lombardi done since Bill Belichick hired him at UNC? A timeline
content:
Bill Belichick was officially hired as North Carolina’s football coach Dec. 11, 2024. Michael Lombardi was his first hire, before he brought any coordinators or position coaches on board.

Belichick named Lombardi the program’s general manager — a new title in college football gaining popularity as roster-building in the sport becomes more professionalized.

Lombardi’s contract pays him $1.5 million, double what many of the top general managers and personnel staffers in college football were being paid. Some have since topped $1 million in annual salary, but Lombardi is still the sport’s highest-paid personnel staffer.

When Belichick brought Lombardi to North Carolina, Lombardi hadn’t worked in football in almost a decade, instead spending much of his time working in media for a variety of outlets and alongside Belichick on the “Coach” podcast.

He hadn’t worked in college football since serving as recruiting coordinator at UNLV from 1981 to 1984.

Here’s a look at some of the notable moments and chapters since his arrival at Chapel Hill:

February 2025: In his introductory news conference, Lombardi said his day looks much like it did when he was working alongside Belichick in the NFL: “Get here early, watch tape, study players, write reports,” he said.

Later in the news conference, he made headlines with a line that’s stuck with UNC, often used pejoratively after the Tar Heels stumbled to a 4-8 debut season and lost to all three in-state rivals for the first time since 1989.

“We consider ourselves the 33rd (NFL) team because everybody who’s involved with our program has had some form or aspect in pro football,” Lombardi said.

April 2025: UNC’s 2025 transfer class featured 41 new players, which ranked ninth nationally, according to 247Sports. The roster churn also included 50 players departing the program.

During the 2025 season, Lombardi and his staff drew criticism from a Group of 5 coach, who spoke on condition of anonymity so he could offer his honest opinions on UNC’s roster-building strategy.

“What I think they miscalculated is with the way they were taking (players) in the portal and paying dudes,” the coach said. “It made me wonder, did they actually understand the landscape they were in? Did they understand that they’re in the ACC, not like Conference USA or the Sun Belt? Like, we got beat by North Carolina on a bunch of kids. I was like, why the f— is North Carolina beating us on kids? When I keep running up against the same P4s over and over again in recruiting, I’m like, all right, they’re going to suck.”

August 2025: According to UNC, Lombardi travelled to Saudi Arabia on “an exploratory fundraising trip.” The school added that Lombardi’s visit was “at the request of a Saudi national who is a college football fan, interested in supporting Coach Belichick.”

October 2025: Lombardi makes more headlines when one of the monthly letters he writes to donors, this one sent out just before North Carolina’s 38-10 loss to Clemson that dropped the Tar Heels to 2-3, is obtained by  FootballScoop.

Lombardi pleaded for patience in the letter and explained that UNC planned to sign around 40 high school prospects in the upcoming class — nearly twice the usual size of a high school signing class — to help turn the program around. He also pointed out that only eight players remained from UNC’s previous four recruiting classes. UNC lost contributors like Howard Sampson to Texas Tech, edge rusher Amare Campbell to Penn State and defensive end Beau Atkinson to Ohio State. The letter also mentioned that coaches like Nick Saban, Lou Holtz, Kirk Ferentz, Jim Harbaugh, Mack Brown and Belichick himself had struggled early before finding success.

“I write to the boosters a lot … when I wrote that letter, I knew it was going to get out,” Lombardi said on the UNC coaches show. “I mean, I’m not an idiot.

“The way it was interpreted, it wasn’t meant to be an excuse. It was just, ‘Hey, here’s where we are.’ And part of the job of a leader is to explain a plan. That’s what I was trying to do is explain the plan.”

December 2025: Lombardi was slated to speak on a panel at the Sports Business Journal’s Intercollegiate Athletics Forum in Las Vegas, an event where conference commissioners and athletic directors publicly discuss and debate issues faced by college sports.

The day before the panel, Lombardi informed SBJ he would not be available to participate.

February 2026: North Carolina’s 2026 recruiting class featured 41 high school players and ranked 19th nationally by the 247Sports Composite. That was third in the ACC, behind only Miami and Florida State. The Tar Heels also added 20 players via the transfer portal. Their transfer class ranked 52nd nationally, 10th in the ACC.

Among the notable moves: UNC signed Wisconsin quarterback Billy Edwards after last year’s headline-making QB signee, Gio Lopez, left for Wake Forest. UNC also signed quarterback Taron Dickens, a transfer from Western Carolina, but he never enrolled and is now slated to play for Northern Illinois.

July 27, 2026: UNC announces Lombardi is placed on administrative leave by the university.

“As is standard procedure with personnel matters, leadership, staff, and student-athletes are prohibited from addressing this topic further, and has no reflection on the merits,” the school said in a statement.

Why Lombardi was placed on leave is unclear.
